definitions.explanation: A steep rock face, especially at the edge of the sea or a mountain.

examples.japanese: {断崖|だんがい}の{上|うえ}からの{景色|けしき}は{絶景|ぜっけい}だった。
examples.english: The view from the top of the cliff was spectacular.

examples.japanese: {波|なみ}が{断崖|だんがい}に{打|う}ちつけていた。
examples.english: Waves were crashing against the cliff.

examples.japanese: {断崖|だんがい}{絶壁|ぜっぺき}の{道|みち}を{慎重|しんちょう}に{歩|ある}いた。
examples.english: I walked carefully along the path on the sheer cliff.

notes:
{断崖|だんがい} refers to a steep cliff or precipice. {断|だん} means 'cut off/sheer' and {崖|がい} means 'cliff.'

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {断崖|だんがい}{絶壁|ぜっぺき}: sheer cliff, precipice
- {断崖|だんがい}から{落|お}ちる: to fall from a cliff
- {海|うみ}の{断崖|だんがい}: sea cliff
- {断崖|だんがい}を{登|のぼ}る: to climb a cliff

FIGURATIVE USE:
- {断崖|だんがい}{絶壁|ぜっぺき}に{立|た}つ: to stand on the edge (of disaster)
- {崖|がけ}っぷち: on the brink/edge

RELATED WORDS:
- {崖|がけ}: cliff (more common in speech)
- {絶壁|ぜっぺき}: precipice, steep cliff
- {岩壁|がんぺき}: rock wall
